opportunities.title: Screening and submittal agent for a 3-recruiter desk running 15 live requisitions
opportunities.problem: Three recruiters (Kathy, Aimee, Lance) cover 15 simultaneously live client requisitions across seven counties, and every candidate arrives as a long free-text web-form application or a phone call rather than structured data. With no ATS or parsing layer visible, reading applications, matching them to req requirements, and preparing a shortlist for client submittal falls entirely on three people, and the req mix (maintenance mechanic, machinist, press set-up, facilities tech, customer service, parts admin) is high-turnover and screening-heavy, so the same work repeats constantly.
evidence: 15 open client requisitions live on the job board, newest pages updated 23 Oct and 2 Nov 2026, spread across South Plainfield, Edison, Mountainside, Old Bridge, Dayton, Elizabeth and Parsippany — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/find-a-job/
Recruiting bench is three people (Senior Recruiters joined 2005 and 2018; Recruiter joined 2019) with no additions after 2019 — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/meet-the-team/

Applications are captured on one long WordPress page (personal details, software proficiency ratings, three employment-history blocks, three references) built with Contact Form 7 / Gravity Forms; no candidate portal or login exists — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/application/
No applicant tracking system or job-board integration is visible; requisitions are plain WordPress pages linked from a single list — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/find-a-job/
Industry brief: reviewing applications and matching applicants to job orders is a Core HR-specialist task (O*NET importance 80 of 100) — https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-1071.00

Industry brief: a staggered rollout of a GenAI support assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 15% on average, with larger gains for less-experienced staff (peer-reviewed, QJE 2025; large-firm call-centre setting, so a transfer not a local measurement) — https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/140/2/889/7990658
opportunities.agent_design: An intake-triage agent that fires the moment a Gravity Forms application or a candidate email lands: it parses the free-text employment history and skills self-ratings, normalises trade terms (e.g. 'press set-up' vs 'press operator'), scores each applicant against the specific req's must-haves, checks licence/Shift availability/travel radius against the worksite town, and writes a one-screen candidate card plus draft client submittal summary into a small internal pipeline board (a lightweight ATS we stand up, since none exists). Recruiters see a ranked queue each morning, click to accept, edit or reject, and only recruiter-approved candidates are submitted to clients. Screening demographics/labels are suppressed from the ranking input and logged, and an adverse-action/human-decision record is written per candidate. Exception path: anything the agent scores below threshold or cannot parse goes to a human with the reason attached.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Off-the-shelf chatbots cannot read a legacy WordPress form, hold a per-requisition scoring rubric, and write structured records into a pipeline that does not exist yet. This needs form-to-pipeline integration, an evaluation harness for trade-role matching, suppressed-field bias logging for EEO exposure, and reliability on a 3-person team with no IT staff — plus the pipeline itself has to be built and maintained.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 6–12 recruiter-hours/week recovered (2–4 hrs per recruiter), i.e. 276–552 hours/yr, worth about $12k–$25k/yr of recruiter time at an assumed $45/hr loaded cost; faster submittal is not dollarised.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Uses NJ median $80,690/yr for HR specialists ($38.79/hr) from the industry brief, verified at O*NET, grossed up modestly to ~$45/hr; assumes 46 working weeks and that only a third to a half of application-reading and shortlisting time is removed. Placement volume and current time-to-submit are not publicly known, so fill-rate gains are excluded — the French public employment service randomised trial (probability of filling posted jobs up 10–15%) is a working paper, not peer-reviewed, and is cited only as directional support, not as a local effect size.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: connect the live application form and inbox to a parsing + scoring agent for the 5 highest-turnover reqs; stand up a minimal internal pipeline board (candidate card, req, stage, notes); run a side-by-side week where recruiters score the same applicants manually to measure agreement and catch misses; deliver a shortlist queue plus an accuracy/bias memo and a go/no-go on rolling out to all 15 reqs.

opportunities.title: NJ Temporary Workers' Bill of Rights placement-packet agent with I-9/E-Verify checklist
opportunities.problem: Every temporary and temp-to-hire placement triggers the same document chain — I-9 verification and E-Verify, assignment details, safety training, optional skills assessments and client-requested background screening — and New Jersey's Temporary Workers' Bill of Rights adds a written assignment notification statement issued at dispatch in English and the worker's primary language, 48-hour notice of schedule/shift/location changes, pay-parity documentation and six-year record retention. For a light-industrial book with high churn, that packet is re-created per placement by recruiters at 8:30–4:00, and a single missing or late notification is both a compliance event and a client-relationship risk.
evidence: FAQ: the firm runs E-Verify for all temporary and temp-to-hire candidates, performs I-9 verification, offers optional safety training and online skills assessments, and adds background screening at client request — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/faqs/

The live requisition mix skews to high-turnover light-industrial and office-support roles (maintenance mechanic, machinist, press set-up, facilities technician, operations admin, customer service, parts administrator), i.e. repeated per-placement paperwork — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/find-a-job/

Industry brief constraint: NJ Temporary Workers' Bill of Rights (fully effective 5 Aug 2023) requires the written assignment notification at dispatch in English and the worker's primary language, 48-hour change notice, pay parity, itemised pay statements and six-year retention; any agent touching placement paperwork must generate accurate, auditable documents. (Law text not independently fetched — search/fetch of NJ DOL pages failed during this task.)
Industry brief: 'hire employees and process hiring-related paperwork' is a Core HR-specialist task at O*NET importance 88 of 100 — https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-1071.00

Industry brief: local labour market is soft (NJ 2025 unemployment 5.2% vs 4.6% in 2024; NJ Professional and Business Services employment down 0.9% YoY in Feb 2026), so margin per placement is under pressure and compliance rework is expensive relative to fee.
opportunities.agent_design: An assignment-lifecycle agent triggered by a placement record (client, worksite, pay rate, shift, start date, worker language). It assembles the packet from templates: bilingual assignment notification, worksite/safety summary, sick-leave and pay-parity notice, and an I-9/E-Verify/training/assessment checklist with per-item status and evidence links. It opens a change-notice workflow — when a client emails or calls a shift or location change, the agent drafts the 48-hour notice in the worker's language, logs the timestamp, and routes it for a recruiter's one-click approval before send. Every packet is versioned and written to a six-year retention store with an audit view. Human approval is mandatory before any document is sent or any pay-affecting change is committed; the agent never finalises I-9 attestation or E-Verify submission itself.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is legally consequential, bilingual, versioned document generation tied to payroll-affecting changes, not a drafting assistant. It needs templates the firm owns, a tamper-evident retention trail, deadline escalation logic, and a system of record that does not exist today — plus PII/SSN and I-9 document handling that argues for a private deployment rather than a public chatbot. A wrong assignment notice is a wage-and-hour exposure, not a typo.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 3–8 hours/week of recruiter and coordinator admin removed (20–40 min per placement packet), about $6k–$17k/yr of time at an assumed $45/hr; the larger but unquantified benefit is eliminated late/missing notices and audit rework. Penalty exposure is not quantified because no dollar figure was sourced.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 150–400 placements per year (derived from three recruiters at roughly 6–14 placements/month each — inferred, not stated anywhere), 20–40 minutes saved per packet and 20–35 minutes per change notice, and 46 working weeks. Assumes bilingual templates can be validated once by counsel rather than re-reviewed per placement.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: draft the bilingual assignment-notification and checklist templates with the recruiters, wire the agent to a simple placement record, run one real month of placements through it in shadow mode (agent drafts, humans still send), then switch on agent-drafted change notices for one client. Deliverables: template set, retention/audit trail, a gap log of every document the current manual process misses, and measured minutes-per-placement before vs after.

opportunities.title: After-hours front door: agent that answers, qualifies and books while the office is closed
opportunities.problem: The single Woodbridge office runs 8:30am–4:00pm weekdays and is closed weekends, and intake is phone-first — the contact page tells visitors to call or complete a form to 'set-up an appointment'. There is no chat, SMS widget, auto-response, booking link or after-hours message anywhere on the site, so every candidate application query or client shift request that lands after 4pm or on a Saturday waits until the next business day, in a business where speed-to-response is the thing reviewers praise most.
evidence: Published hours Monday–Friday 8:30am–4:00pm, weekends closed; contact page asks visitors to call 732-750-5600 or complete a form to set up an appointment — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/contact-us/
No live chat, chatbot, SMS widget or click-to-text feature is present anywhere on the site, and no online scheduling or appointment booking exists — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/

On-site testimonials (about 19) repeatedly credit named recruiters for fast response by phone, text and email and quick interview turnaround, so responsiveness is the firm's stated differentiator — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/reviews/
Recruiters publish direct dials and personal company emails, and candidates are expected to come in and be interviewed in one visit — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/meet-the-team/

Industry brief: a GenAI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 15% on average in a large call-centre deployment (QJE 2025, peer-reviewed; different setting, so treated as directional only) — https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/140/2/889/7990658
opportunities.agent_design: A web + inbound-email/voicemail-to-text agent that acts as the after-hours desk: it answers questions about open reqs, hours, what to bring for I-9, pay range and the application steps from the firm's own pages and FAQ; it captures structured candidate intake (name, trade, shift preference, travel radius, availability) and writes it to the same pipeline as the screening agent; it books interview slots directly into the recruiters' calendars inside the 8:30–4:00 window; and for client-side messages it books a callback and pages the on-call recruiter only for genuine shift-coverage emergencies. It never quotes a bill rate, never confirms a placement commitment, and never discusses pay parity or assignment terms — those are routed to a recruiter with a summary and a drafted reply. Full transcripts land in a nightly digest so nothing is silently lost.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A website chat plugin cannot read the live requisition pages, apply the specific eligibility rules (E-Verify, I-9, shift/commute constraints), write into the internal pipeline, or hold a do-not-say list around rates and assignment terms. It also has to behave predictably at 2am with nobody watching, across both candidate and client intents, and hand off cleanly — that is workflow, escalation design and monitoring, not a subscription widget.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 1–3 hours/week of routine inquiry handling removed, about $2k–$4k/yr at an assumed $23/hr, plus 2–5 additional qualified candidates and 1–3 client inquiries per week captured that would otherwise wait for the next business day (value not dollarised — conversion to placement is unknown).
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 3–8 after-hours inquiries per week (inferred from phone-first intake and a 4pm close — no traffic or call-volume data is published), 15–25 minutes of handling avoided per inquiry, 46 working weeks, and $22.95/hr NJ median for customer service representatives (from the industry brief, not independently re-fetched). Excludes any revenue from captured leads, which cannot be estimated without inquiry volume and conversion rates.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: deploy one agent on the site plus the generic inbox and after-hours voicemail, scoped to candidates first (req questions + intake + interview booking) and clients second (callback booking). Deliverables: a knowledge base built from the FAQ, services, application and req pages; an escalation and do-not-say policy; a nightly digest; and a measured count of after-hours inquiries captured vs the previous four weeks' baseline.

lead_score.rationale: Pain is well evidenced and specific: 15 live requisitions against three long-tenured recruiters, no ATS or candidate portal, a single long web form as the only structured intake, phone-first contact with a 4pm close, and a compliance-heavy NJ placement packet repeated per hire; the req mix is high-churn light-industrial work that regenerates all of it. Fit is strong across A (intake, screening, scheduling, placement paperwork) and D (the pipeline board that does not exist), with C as a thin layer for FAQ/assignment questions — no hardware or edge AI need, so E is out. Ability to pay is the weak link: a family-owned 11–50 person single-office agency with undisclosed revenue, thin staffing margins, a softening NJ market (5.2% unemployment, Professional and Business Services down 0.9% YoY) and no published owner or GM, so the economic buyer, budget and placement volume are all unknown and any engagement will be small and price-sensitive. Ease is middling: one office, a small stable team and no legacy systems to unseat make a pilot fast, but the absence of an ATS means we must build the system of record, and the buyer has to be found by walking in. Strategic value is high: NJ temp-staffing compliance paperwork plus a no-ATS screening stack is a near-identical package for thousands of small NJ/NY staffing agencies, and the compliance template is reusable as-is. Net 72 — a credible, high-fit first client that needs a small paid pilot and a walk-in conversation with whoever actually owns the firm, not a large transformation sale.

best_evidence_signal: 15 concurrently live client requisitions across seven NJ counties handled by a three-person recruiting team with no ATS, no candidate portal and no after-hours intake — https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/find-a-job/ (with https://www.premierpersonnelgroup.com/meet-the-team/)
